links.outcome: LLM-generated vs original physician requisition histories: completeness, quality, radiologist preference, perceived harm
links.effect: LLM histories more often included primary diagnosis (99.5% vs 89%), acute symptoms (15% vs 4%), surgery (61% vs 12%); radiologists preferred LLM histories 89% vs 5%; lower likelihood of harm 3% vs 55%.
links.quote: Compared with original requisition histories, LLM-generated histories were more complete and were preferred by radiologists for imaging interpretation and perceived safety.

links.outcome: Radiologist review of LLM-generated histories against reference standard and original histories for quality and harm
links.effect: GPT-4 extracted oncologic parameters from clinical notes with F1 = 0.983; 10 radiologists preferred LLM histories 89% vs 5% and rated lower likelihood of harm (3% vs 55%).
links.quote: Radiologists preferred LLM-generated histories for imaging interpretation (89% vs 5%, 7% equal; P < .001), indicating they would enable more complete interpretation (86% vs 0%, 15% equal; P < .001) and have a lower likelihood of harm (3% vs 55%, 42% neither; P < .001).

unlisted_practices: Using LLMs to draft structured clinical histories for imaging requisitions from EHR notes to fill documentation gaps

screen.reason: Evaluates GPT-4 to generate clinical histories from EHR notes for oncologic imaging requisitions, evaluated offline against ground truth and in a reader preference study by 10 radiologists.
